clue.text: Charge over line — that makes sense

parts.note: a charge is a fee
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a fee placed over a line item as a sensible arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something is to perceive it, a straightforward synonym of the verb sense.

clue.text: Carried on, initially, in island

parts.note: past participle of bear, to carry

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of on

explanation.surface: Something was carried on to an island, as if describing cargo arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

clue.text: Horse-drawn vehicle, something one aims to avoid when driving

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light two-wheeled carriage

definitions.text: something one aims to avoid when driving
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a speed camera set-up that catches motorists

explanation.surface: A carriage that drivers hope to steer clear of on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is the speed trap that a motorist hopes not to be caught in.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is both a small pony carriage and a police speed check catching motorists.

clue.text: Computer on which option from menu shouldn't be dropped?

definitions.text: Computer on which option from menu shouldn't be dropped?

parts.words: Computer on which option from menu shouldn't be dropped?
parts.note: surface reading: a computer menu option that must not be removed

parts.words: option from menu shouldn't be dropped
parts.note: setter's reading: a portable machine resting on your knees while you eat, so no food from a restaurant menu should fall on it

explanation.surface: A software menu option that ought never to be deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Menu' and 'option' sound like computer terms, but the menu is a food menu and the dish is spilt on a machine balanced on the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable computer used on one's knees while seated, where spilt food would be a hazard.

clue.text: Corrupt son's ruse that leaves a bad taste in the mouth

definitions.text: that leaves a bad taste in the mouth
definitions.note: read as 'quality that leaves a bad taste', a noun

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoiled and altered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishonest son's trick leaves everyone with an unpleasant feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourness is an acid taste and, figuratively, the bitterness left by bad behaviour.

clue.text: Doctor chatted about soldiers in separate unit

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged word surrounds the next piece
to doctor is to tamper with, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
soldiers are men in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A medic gossiped about the troops serving in a separate unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person who chatted, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a group of troops sent away from the main body for a particular task.

clue.text: Performing relatively well on course, or rather poorly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on a golf course, taking fewer strokes than the standard is good
second meaning: feeling a bit unwell

explanation.surface: A golfer seems to be doing well, or perhaps badly, a paradoxical report.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, par is the expected number of strokes, so scoring under it is good, while the everyday idiom means off-colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means under the standard score in golf and, idiomatically, slightly ill.

clue.text: Parking briefly, it's to add petrol primarily?

definitions.text: Parking briefly, it's to add petrol primarily?

indicators.note: briefly cuts the word before it down to a single initial, as in an abbreviation

parts.note: P is the parking sign
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of petrol

explanation.surface: A short halt in a racing pit lane to refuel the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a brief parking whose main purpose is refuelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is a racing car's brief halt for fuel and tyres, the whole clue describing it.

clue.text: Part of what one does is made up

indicators.note: part of tells you the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: inside wh-at one d-oes

explanation.surface: Something one does turns out to be invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' suggests invented, but it means made amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make up for a wrong, making amends for it.

clue.text: Mercury, for instance, showing temperature with level

parts.note: a plane is a flat, level surface
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A mercury thermometer shows the temperature level.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury looks like the metal in a thermometer, but it is the world nearest the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the innermost planet of the solar system, an example of the category.

clue.text: Saint subject to criticism? That's child's play

parts.note: St Peter the apostle
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Criticising a saint is said to be easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's play' sounds like an easy task, but it is a stage play for children.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan is a famous play written for children, staged every Christmas.

clue.text: Words as repeated by another from crazy prophet's decree

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone passes on the words of a mad prophet's pronouncement.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect speech is the grammatical form in which another person's words are relayed rather than quoted.

clue.text: Out? I'm not, and very happy about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the happy word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: elated means overjoyed
answering the question 'Out?': if I'm not out, I'm in

explanation.surface: Asked whether they are out, someone denies it and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm not' answers 'Out?', so the speaker is in: I'M IN goes inside ELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A player or contestant who is eliminated is out of the game or competition.

clue.text: How to treat wound that makes doctor persist, ignoring odds?

definitions.note: verb sense: to treat a wound

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: ignoring odds means skipping the odd-numbered positions and keeping the even ones

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of persist

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps going when treating an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to clean it and cover it with a bandage.

clue.text: Business unlikely to yield much

definitions.meaning: second meaning: solid, not giving way under pressure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' suggests profits from a business, but it means give way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a company and an adjective for something solid that resists pressure.

clue.text: Reasonable manner and pace

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Describes a sensible approach and a steady speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means not extreme, within sensible limits, close in sense to reasonable.

clue.text: Journalists with Trump, say, shortly heading south

indicators.note: shortly asks for a word to be cut short, losing its ending

parts.note: Donald Trump is an example of a US head of state

indicators.note: heading means the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: first letter of south

explanation.surface: Reporters travel with Trump as he heads south shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is the collective term for newspapers and the reporters who work for them.

clue.text: Sink warship north of port, for example

parts.note: a submarine is a warship
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Instructions to sink a warship lying north of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of' in a down clue puts the first piece above the second. 'Port' suggests a harbour but means the ship's left side.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink lower or settle, as ground or floodwater does.

clue.text: Part of act heard and understood

indicators.note: heard tells you to go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a scene is a division of an act in a play

explanation.surface: Part of a stage act was heard and taken in by the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I've seen' is used to mean 'I understand', as in 'I see'.

clue.text: Total unity as Asian country cut requirement for sight-seeing

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the country's name loses its last letter

parts.note: India is a country in Asia
you need to be able to see clearly to look at sights

explanation.surface: A nation's unity is likened to clear views for tourists in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sight-seeing' suggests tourism, but read literally it is seeing at all, which needs good visibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Indivisibility is the state of being unable to be split, complete oneness.

clue.text: Class of sounds, all used in audiometry

parts.words: Class of sounds, all used in audiometry
parts.note: surface reading: a category of sounds tested in hearing examinations
setter's reading: the word audiometry happens to contain every one of the letters A, E, I, O, U

explanation.surface: A category of tones that are all played in a hearing test.
explanation.walkthrough: Audiometry is hearing testing, which suggests sounds being played, but the point is that its spelling includes each of the five letters of this class.
explanation.definitionFit: Vowels are speech sounds made with an open vocal tract, a recognised class of phonemes.

clue.text: Kind of paper that's taken in chemistry test

definitions.meaning: first meaning: indicator paper that turns red or blue
second meaning: a test of acidity, and figuratively any decisive test

explanation.surface: A type of paper used in a school chemistry experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is a dye on paper that shows acid or alkali, and a litmus test is a decisive check.

clue.text: An error, stupidly, about weight, being less fat

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
stupidly suggests something done without sense, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A dieter made a silly mistake about their weight, though slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrower means slimmer, of smaller width, the comparative of a word for thin.

clue.text: Conclusions reached by teacher, sadly, about work of poor quality

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the selected letters go round the next piece
conclusions are endings, so take the final letter of each of the following words

parts.note: final letters of teacher and sadly
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A teacher's sad verdict on a pupil's poor piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Ropy is British informal slang for shoddy or below par.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British slang for shoddy, inferior or in bad condition.

clue.text: How diplomacy is shown to be complete

parts.note: describes the manner, as in 'in haste'
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A question about how diplomatic skill proves itself whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' asks for a manner: someone using diplomacy acts with it, or 'in' it, the way one acts in haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means undamaged and whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Rebel following master in preparation of courses

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary
F is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: A rebel follows a master during the preparation of lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like part of the wordplay that the rebel follows, but it starts the definition; 'courses' are meal courses, not lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is an expert cook who prepares the dishes of a meal.

clue.text: Pulse is one fifty, following fast time

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the numerals are placed behind the fasting season rather than ahead of it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
Roman numeral one
Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A heart rate reading of one hundred and fifty after a quick sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the numerals after the fasting season. 'Pulse' suggests heartbeat, but means an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible legume seed, and pulses are the dried seeds of such plants.

clue.text: Began again after page is taken as read

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
to resume is to begin again

explanation.surface: Reading started again after a page was assumed to have been read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the restarting word behind the page abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be presumed is to be assumed true without proof, the meaning of the idiom taken as read.
